Implementation inference from [PyTorch SDPA](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention/): compute causal SASRec states and history key/value projections once. For K candidates per supervised position, flatten candidate queries to [B,LK,d]; apply explicit mask M[b,tK+c,j]=(j≤t) AND nonpadding[b,j], with is_causal=False. Position t predicts the next item, so history includes t. SDPA boolean True means allowed. Chunk supervised queries to limit attention memory; arithmetic remains O(BL²Kd). Prefix reuse means sharing causal states/projections, rather than rerunning SASRec for every prefix. These states match separately encoded prefixes only when truncation and positional indexing match. Candidate-only queries additionally permit reusing candidate/history logits across prefixes; position-dependent queries generally do not.

For full-catalog inference, cache each user’s final history projections and score candidate chunks [B,C,d], reducing attention workspace to O(BCL). Normalize each candidate over history positions, never across candidates; chunking then preserves mathematical scores, subject to floating-point differences. Disable evaluation dropout explicitly. For empty histories, temporarily allow one dummy zero key/value, then zero the resulting context; this prevents all-masked softmax NaNs, a problem discussed in the [PyTorch tutorial](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/intermediate/transformer_building_blocks.html). Zeroing NaNs afterward is insufficient for reliable gradients.

[ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) supports a scalar gate initialized to zero. For s=s_base+αrθ, differentiation gives ∂loss/∂θ=α(∂loss/∂s)(∂r/∂θ), initially zero, while ∂loss/∂α=(∂loss/∂s)rθ can be nonzero. Keep the residual computation in autograd even at α=0; skipping it prevents gate learning. Avoid simultaneously zeroing the residual output. Runtime feasibility requires measurement; batching and caching alone cannot establish budget compliance.
